user.title: Where are you watching from?
user.description: Passes are predicted for this location. It defaults to your Home Assistant home location and never leaves your Home Assistant instance (unless you add an N2YO API key in the options).

data_description.name: Used as the device name, for example "ISS" or "ISS at the cabin".
data_description.elevation: Height of the location in metres. A rough value is fine.

reconfigure.title: Move this location
reconfigure.description: Correct where passes are predicted for. The location keeps its entities, and the dashboard cards that show it keep working.

data_description.elevation: Height of the location in metres. A rough value is fine.

error.invalid_location: Enter a latitude between -90° and 90° and a valid longitude.

abort.already_configured: This location is already set up.

data.show_in_sidebar: Show ISS Tracker in the sidebar

data_description.min_elevation: The station only counts as visible above this elevation. 10° clears most trees and rooftops.
data_description.min_peak_elevation: Skip low passes that never climb higher than this.
data_description.max_sun_elevation: The Sun must be at least this far below the horizon. -6° is the end of civil twilight; use -3° for brighter twilight passes.
data_description.min_visible_duration: Skip passes visible for less than this.
data_description.forecast_days: How far ahead to predict. Timing more than a week ahead can shift by minutes as new orbit data arrives; predictions are refined automatically.
data_description.alert_lead_minutes: The "Visible pass soon" sensor turns on this long before the station appears.
data_description.show_in_sidebar: Adds an ISS Tracker page to the sidebar with a 3D globe, the station's course and a countdown to the next visible pass. The globe is also available as a dashboard card either way.
data_description.n2yo_api_key: Optional. Adds N2YO as a backup source of orbit data and compares N2YO's predictions with this integration's once a day.

error.n2yo_unreachable: Could not reach N2YO to check the API key. Try again later.
error.peak_below_mask: The minimum peak elevation cannot be lower than the horizon mask.

elements_stale.title: ISS predictions are paused
elements_stale.description: The cached orbital elements for the International Space Station are {age} days old, and no fresher ones could be downloaded ({error}). Predictions older than this would be misleading, so the ISS Pass Prediction entities are unavailable until a download succeeds. Check that Home Assistant can reach celestrak.org or wheretheiss.at; adding an N2YO API key in the options gives a further source. This message goes away by itself once fresh elements arrive.
